sections.title: The Two Witnesses
observations: In this section, we encounter the two witnesses who are given authority to prophesy for 1,260 days, symbolizing a period of divine witness and testimony amidst opposition.
The imagery of sackcloth suggests mourning and repentance, indicating the seriousness of their message in a time of judgment.
These witnesses are often interpreted as representing the faithful church or specific prophetic figures, emphasizing the theme of God's protection over His people during tribulation.

sections.title: The Seventh Trumpet
observations: The blowing of the seventh trumpet marks a significant transition in the narrative, heralding the final judgments and the establishment of God's kingdom.
The declaration that the kingdom of the world has become the kingdom of our Lord emphasizes God's sovereignty and the ultimate victory of Christ.
This section also highlights the response of the nations and the judgment that follows, reinforcing the theme of accountability before God.

importantVerses.commentary: The two witnesses are empowered to prophesy, highlighting God's provision of testimony even in dark times.
The proclamation of the kingdom of God signifies the culmination of redemptive history and the reign of Christ.

questions: What is the significance of the two witnesses in the context of the church's mission today?
How do the events of the seventh trumpet relate to the overall theme of God's sovereignty in Revelation?
In what ways can we understand the mourning of the witnesses as a reflection of the current state of the world?
